notes:
=== SessionGopher — Remote Access Tool Credential Extraction ===
Sweeps PuTTY, WinSCP, FileZilla, SuperPuTTY, and RDP saved session credentials from registry.

=== WHAT SESSIONGOPHER EXTRACTS ===
PuTTY: HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions → hostname, username, proxy credentials
WinSCP: HKCU\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions → hostname, username, password (encrypted with reversible key)
FileZilla: %APPDATA%\FileZilla\sitemanager.xml and recentservers.xml → hostname, user, plaintext passwords
SuperPuTTY: %APPDATA%\SuperPuTTY\Sessions.XML → decrypted session data
RDP: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers → recently connected RDP hosts

=== USAGE ===
Without local admin (current user only):
  Import-Module .\SessionGopher.ps1
  Invoke-SessionGopher

With local admin (all users on system):
  Invoke-SessionGopher -AllDomain   → searches HKEY_USERS for all user SIDs
  Invoke-SessionGopher -Thorough    → also searches drives for .ppk, .rdp, .sdtid files

Remote sweep (with credentials):
  Invoke-SessionGopher -Target dc01 -u domain\admin -p Password123

=== KEY CREDENTIAL STORES ===
.ppk files (PuTTY Private Key) → SSH key material → convert with puttygen → SSH access
.rdp files → saved RDP connections, may contain encoded credentials
.sdtid files (RSA SecurID) → MFA tokens for VPN/authentication systems

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
SessionGopher on admin workstation → PuTTY sessions to servers → SSH credentials
WinSCP credentials → FTP/SFTP access to file servers → data access or further lateral movement
RDP saved sessions list → map of what servers this user accesses → priority targets for lateral movement
After local admin escalation → run with -AllDomain to sweep all users on the system

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
PuTTY sessions saved by sysadmins → SSH access to Linux/Unix servers
WinSCP saved sessions → file transfer to/from servers (often includes credentials for SFTP)
FileZilla XML files → plaintext credentials (FileZilla stores in cleartext by design)
PPK files anywhere on filesystem → SSH key material without passphrase = immediate access

recommended.note: Reuse any saved Windows creds you find.

name: Credential Hunting - SessionGopher
description: SessionGopher extracts saved session secrets for PuTTY, WinSCP, FileZilla, SuperPuTTY, and RDP from the registry and user profiles.

defense.why_it_works: SessionGopher queries registry keys and files used by remote administration tools (PuTTY, WinSCP, SuperPuTTY, FileZilla, RDP) to extract saved session parameters and credentials. These tools often store credentials in the HKCU registry or in app-specific configuration files, recoverable without cracking.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as the target user (HKCU keys accessible). SessionGopher.ps1 loaded. For domain-wide sweep: admin rights for remote WMI access to other machines.
defense.impact: Mass recovery of saved SSH, SFTP, FTP, and RDP credentials from all remote admin tools used by the compromised user. May reveal credentials for servers, jump hosts, and network equipment.
defense.detection: SessionGopher.ps1 import and execution. Registry reads across PuTTY/WinSCP/FileZilla HKCU paths. SIEM: alert on SessionGopher execution by standard user. EDR: script execution with credential harvesting behavior.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell: Import-Module SessionGopher.ps1 | HKCU registry reads across multiple remote-tool paths | Process log: Invoke-SessionGopher executed
defense.prevention: Avoid saving credentials in remote management tools — use password managers or SSH agent forwarding instead. Apply HKCU registry auditing on PuTTY/WinSCP paths. Use endpoint protection to block known credential harvesting scripts.
defense.misconfiguration: PuTTY or WinSCP sessions saved with passwords for convenience on a workstation accessible to low-privileged users. No restriction on accessing other users' session data.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# SessionGopher extracts from PuTTY, WinSCP, FileZilla:
Import-Module .\SessionGopher.ps1
Invoke-SessionGopher -Target WINLPE-SRV01
# Output: SSH session to 10.129.1.10 as root, password: Sup3rS3cur3!
defense.secure_config:
# Do not save passwords in PuTTY/WinSCP
# Use SSH key authentication instead
# PuTTY: Connection > SSH > Auth > Private key file

# Remove saved passwords
reg delete HKCU\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions /va /f

# Enforce SSH key-only authentication on servers:
# sshd_config: PasswordAuthentication no
defense.evasion: Copy the credential store (browser Login Data, .kdbx, PSReadline history) and decrypt/crack it OFFLINE rather than running signatured binaries (LaZagne/SharpChrome) on the host; scope searches to likely paths to limit disk I/O; use built-in cmdlets over dropped tools.
